documents.implementation_surface: Phase 00 traceability, milestone, terminology, safety-performance, change-control, and document-coverage validators.
accepted_behavior: Language, compiler platform, and execution ecosystem remain distinct identities connected by artifacts.
Profiles are compile-time contracts that decide legal forms, effects, capabilities, allocation, unsafe boundaries, and target lowerings before backend emission.
Safe Gravity dangerous operations use one of the four D8 outcomes and artifacts retain provenance.
rejected_behavior: One universal runtime as the language definition.
Host-language semantics as Gravity semantics.
Unsafe behavior invisible to the artifact graph.
Self-hosting claims without reproducible stage evidence.
conformance_criteria: Document sequence preserves D0 dependency order.
Every profile has positive and negative fixtures.
Every emitted artifact records profile, target, source identity, compiler identity, effects, capabilities, safety status, and provenance.
Every bootstrap stage records compiler identity, source hash, artifact hash, and equivalence evidence.

documents.implementation_surface: Contract traceability and document coverage records for canonical pipeline boundaries.
accepted_behavior: Reader, macro expansion, semantic checks, MIR, domain IRs, optimization, lowering, emission, and provenance expose equivalent pass facts.
Domain IRs keep semantic anchors to typed core or MIR.
Runtime selection follows profile and target instead of ambient compiler defaults.
rejected_behavior: Backend receiving unchecked source or core.
Domain IR artifact without semantic anchor.
Runtime service selected as an implicit default.
conformance_criteria: Pipeline fixtures expose required facts before consuming passes.
Domain artifacts include typed-core or MIR anchors.
Runtime manifests show services selected by profile and target.

documents.implementation_surface: Milestone evidence system and roadmap evidence ledgers.
accepted_behavior: Every milestone compiles something real, rejects something real, emits artifacts, and records diagnostics before support is claimed.
Later work can start early only through documented interfaces without claiming release status.
Release evidence bundles name governing documents, fixtures, diagnostics, artifacts, profile and capability matrices, safety reports, reproducibility records, and open risks.
rejected_behavior: Milestone claim without positive or negative fixtures.
Downstream feature claim before upstream contracts exist.
Safety, profile, or capability checks deferred after executable support is claimed.
Code emitted without required provenance or conformance artifacts.
conformance_criteria: Hosted hello release compiles and runs only with evidence.
Typed core and effect artifacts are emitted before typed-core support is claimed.
Profile, effect, and capability illegal combinations are rejected.
Self-hosting trust is not retired without reproducible equivalence evidence.

documents.implementation_surface: Diagnostic namespace registry and terminology boundary validator.
accepted_behavior: Compiler, runtime, package, tooling, and governance artifacts use stable D3 names for profile, target, effect, capability, safety mode, and provenance.
Diagnostics report stable concepts rather than backend-specific approximations.
Domain-specific documents map concepts to source forms, typed core, MIR, domain IRs, artifacts, effects, and capabilities.
rejected_behavior: Profile and target conflation.
Effect and capability conflation.
Runtime and backend conflation.
Artifact identity reduced to a file path.
Unsafe behavior described without audit tracking.
conformance_criteria: Critical pre-implementation documents use D3 terms with D3 meanings.
Compiler diagnostics and artifact manifests use D3 concept names.
Documentation checks reject ambiguous normative terminology.

documents.implementation_surface: Document coverage records and traceability links for domain coverage claims.
accepted_behavior: Coverage claims name domain, profile set, accepted subset, required effects and capabilities, emitted artifact family, and credible replacement slice.
Universal syntax, effects, capability requirements, diagnostics, and artifact provenance remain recognizable across domains.
Interop boundaries are typed, effect-annotated, capability-gated, profile-legal, audited if unsafe, artifacted, and fixture-covered.
rejected_behavior: Hidden universal runtime.
Host reflection in constrained profiles.
Dynamic eval in kernel, firmware, hardware, or core profiles.
Simulated domain examples without real domain effects.
Target artifacts without provenance.
conformance_criteria: Domain documents include accepted and rejected canonical fixtures.
Domain fixtures compile through standard syntax, profile checking, type/effect checking, safety analysis, and artifact emission.
Coverage reports distinguish implemented, designed, delegated, and out-of-scope slices.

documents.implementation_surface: Document coverage records and change-control ambiguity log for replacement claim discipline.
accepted_behavior: Replacement claims specify incumbent family, Gravity profiles, targets, supported slice, unsupported slice, interop boundaries, artifacts, tests, and performance expectations.
Interop preserves types, effects, capabilities, ownership, provenance, and safety boundaries.
Migration replaces unsafe or low-level logic only after audit records and negative fixtures exist.
rejected_behavior: Broad replacement claim without a named slice.
Interop boundary without type, effect, capability, ownership, or provenance metadata.
Replacement record lacking behavior, safety, performance, or tooling evidence.
Generated or migrated unsafe code without unsafe island.
conformance_criteria: Every replacement claim has a replacement slice record.
Every interop boundary is represented as a typed artifact.
Replacement docs distinguish implemented, delegated, experimental, and unsupported behavior.

accepted_behavior: Performance starts from safe semantics and erases only checks whose proof survives.
Performance claims name profile, target, runtime, backend, safety mode, layout, input domain, erased checks, proof obligations, and benchmark method.
Optimization either preserves a fact, regenerates a fact, retains a runtime check, or rejects the transformation.
rejected_behavior: Optimization based on undefined behavior.
Silent fast math.
Dropping capability checks without proof and policy.
Target-specific assumptions missing from artifacts.
Benchmarks without reproducible harness and baseline.
conformance_criteria: Optimizer fixtures show preserved, regenerated, retained, and rejected safety facts.
Check-elision tests cover bounds, overflow, initialization, capability, taint, and replay checks.
Benchmark artifacts are reproducible from source hash, compiler identity, target fingerprint, and harness.

documents.implementation_surface: Document coverage records for extension manifest and pass-contract obligations.
accepted_behavior: Extensions declare kind, owner, input contract, output contract, profiles, effects, capabilities, safety mode, artifact schema, fixtures, diagnostics, version, and compatibility policy.
Macros transform syntax objects and preserve provenance.
Compiler passes declare preserved, invalidated, and regenerated facts with proof obligations and artifacts.
rejected_behavior: Compiler internal mutation outside pass contracts.
Text transformation claiming macro status.
Effects without declarations.
Authority outside grants.
Unsafe safe API without wrapper proof and audit.
Hermetic build effects without grants.
conformance_criteria: Each extension kind has a manifest schema.
Macro extension fixtures prove hygiene, provenance, and profile legality.
Provider fixtures prove profile support and rejected unsupported profiles.
Hermetic build fixtures reject unauthorized build effects.

documents.implementation_surface: Safety-performance gate model, change-control workflow, and safety diagnostics.
accepted_behavior: Every dangerous operation has exactly one outcome: :proven-safe, :runtime-checked, :rejected, or :unsafe-island.
Unsafe islands include reason, source span, profiles, effects, capabilities, preconditions, postconditions, invariants, safe boundary, evidence, owner, review, and re-review policy.
Optimizations preserve, regenerate, retain, or reject safety checks.
rejected_behavior: Trust the backend safety.
Unsafe-by-default systems profiles.
Host-runtime checks as only evidence for lower profiles.
Unchecked FFI in safe code.
Optimizer check erasure without proof.
AI tool authority based on prompt text instead of grants.
conformance_criteria: Each safety family has positive, negative, and unsafe-island fixtures.
Safe code fixtures never require target undefined behavior.
Unsafe island extraction produces stable audit artifacts.
Optimizer fixtures demonstrate preserved proof or residual checks.

documents.implementation_surface: Milestone evidence, safety-performance, change-control, and document coverage validators.
accepted_behavior: Safety-critical, math-critical, optimization-critical, replay-critical, unsafe, package, and bootstrap claims produce explicit evidence.
Proof or certificate records name claim, domain, assumptions, checker, inputs, and result.
Optimization cannot erase checks or proof obligations without replacement evidence.
Bootstrap verification is reproducible from recorded inputs.
rejected_behavior: Prose-only proof claims.
EML normalization presented as equality without proof.
Benchmark results presented as correctness evidence.
Test snapshots presented as proof certificates.
Self-hosting trust without reproducible stage comparison.
conformance_criteria: Approximation fixtures include accepted and rejected certificates.
MIR verifier fixtures catch malformed control flow, missing type facts, missing effect facts, and invalid profile facts.
Optimization fixtures show preserved or regenerated proof evidence.
Bootstrap fixtures compare stage outputs and explain permitted differences.
